question: A student claims: "If a charged particle moves through a region where **only a magnetic field** is present with constant velocity, then the magnetic field in that region must be zero." Evaluate the validity of this statement.

options.A: True; constant velocity implies net force is zero, so the magnetic field must be zero.
options.B: True; constant velocity is possible only if an electric field is also present to cancel the magnetic force.
options.C: False; the magnetic field can be non-zero if the particle moves parallel to the magnetic field.
options.D: False; the magnetic field must be non-zero to cancel the effect of gravity.
